line: Level 1: The Rumour Dungeon
Anecdote Bat and Echo Chamber Wisp, test this claim.
Slime of Misinformation: "Nobody ever measured that. You can't check it, so believe it!"
Measured for 36 people.
explain: There is enough data to put this claim to the test.

line: Rumour Goblin: "Everyone online says it's true. Popularity is proof!"
Raw link between carbs and the rise: r = +0.76 (95% CI +0.73 to +0.79).
explain: The raw data leans the way the rumour says. Interesting, but a pattern is not proof yet.

line: Anecdote Bat: "It worked for my cousin, so it works for everyone!"
Worth the credits. I'll check it properly.
The pattern holds within 100% of 36 people's own meals.
explain: It holds for most individuals, not just one anecdote.

line: Echo Chamber Wisp: "Your claim is just carbs, repeated back to you in a new costume."
Worth the credits. I'll check it properly.

line: Level 2: The Forgotten Archives
Confounding Phantom and Small Sample Skeleton, test this claim.
Preprint Mimic: "This promising preprint says your claim improves predictions. Trust it!"
Adding carbs changes prediction error by +7.47 mg/dL per meal (95% CI +6.61 to +8.30) across 36 people.
explain: Predictions for people left out of fitting improve, and the whole range is above zero.

line: Small Sample Skeleton: "Your average is carried by a handful of people."
Worth the credits. I'll check it properly.
100% of 36 people are predicted better.
explain: Most people benefit, not just a lucky few.

line: Confounding Phantom: "Your effect is really something else hiding behind it."
Worth the credits. I'll check it properly.
Raw direction: positive. After accounting for carbs: positive.
explain: The direction survives adjusting for carbs.

line: Level 3: The Temple of Replication
Contradiction Wraith and Selection Bias, test this claim.
Replication Sentinel: "Show me it works in groups of people you did not fit it on."
Replicated in 5 of 5 independent groups of people.
explain: It works in groups of people it was never fitted on.

line: Contradiction Wraith: "A second glucose sensor tells a different story."
Worth the credits. I'll check it properly.
By sensor: libre +7.47, dexcom +7.49 mg/dL per meal.
explain: Both sensors agree.

line: Overfitting: "OVERFITTING! Scrambled data could have done just as well."
0 of 200 scrambled copies did as well (p = 0.005).
explain: The real data beat almost every scrambled copy: unlikely to be luck.

line: Selection Bias: "SELECTION BIAS! Remove your best cases and it vanishes."
I must save my credits for the trials ahead.
explain: Skipping a check saves credits, but the claim stays unverified.
